beats.narration_text: A skill is a folder Claude reads before it works. This one is explore-data. Its SKILL.md file holds the full instruction set, in plain language — no hidden logic. Claude reads it, then acts. The file is the program.
The instructions are laid out in a Steps section. Claude reads each step in order and runs it — linear, no branching unless a step says otherwise.

Here's the actual job: profile a dataset to understand its shape, quality, and patterns. Check null rates and column distributions, spot issues like duplicates or suspicious values, and decide which dimensions and metrics are worth analyzing next.
Ask it to explore your data, and explore-data hands back a profile — shape, quality, patterns, and the issues worth flagging — the same checklist every time, not a freeform report.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Paste this into Claude: I have a CSV of customer orders. Profile it for me — how many rows and columns, which columns have missing values and how often, whether any rows look like duplicates, and which two or three columns are most worth digging into next. Walk me through your plan before you start. That clause matters — explaining first surfaces the real constraint logic.
